problem: The clause 'shrinks the depletion width so the drain reaches deeper' is backwards. Heavier body doping shrinks the depletion widths, including the drain junction depletion width, so the drain field penetrates less, not deeper. This is exactly why halo/pocket doping is used to fight short-channel effects. As written, a student learns the opposite of the standard mechanism.
fix: Heavier body doping raises junction leakage and junction capacitance and cuts mobility. It does shrink the depletion widths and so helps contain the drain field, but it costs mobility and off-state junction leakage, and it stops working once the body must be thin.

problem: 'Fin pitch' and 'fin pitch' based cell layout are used without definition, and 'work function' is used in Section 2 without a one-line reminder of what it means. A reader meeting these first here has to guess.
fix: Add one line: fin pitch is the centre-to-centre distance between two neighbouring fins (nm); work function is the energy needed to pull an electron out of the gate metal, measured in eV.

problem: The answer gives only a partial mechanism ('drain field acts on few carriers'), which can be read as if the drain still controls the channel just with fewer carriers. The main reason a thin fully depleted body helps is that the drain field lines end on the nearby gate instead of spreading through the body, so the barrier near the source barely moves.
fix: Answer: in a thin fully depleted body the gate is very close to every part of the channel, so most drain field lines terminate on the gate instead of on the body. The drain can shift little charge, the source barrier stays fixed, and drain-induced barrier lowering is small.
